data.name: Celene
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'selene', meaning 'moon'. In Greek mythology, Selene was the goddess of the moon, revered for her cyclical nature and the influence she had on tides and growth.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine and the cyclical nature of life.
data.cultural_impact: Celene, as a name, invokes the image of the moon goddess Selene, that decorated pottery, coins, and architecture in ancient Greece. She was associated with the creative cycle of life, and the name Celene could encourage a sense of artistic imagery, inspiration, and connection to the natural world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Celene holds relevance to the spiritual realm as it comes from the ancient Greek mythology of Selene, the goddess of the moon. Naming a child Celene could represent a desire to encourage an enchanted, imaginative spirit and emphasize the connection to the ebb and flow of nature and its cycles. In Christianity, it could also be seen as a reminder of the cyclical nature of life, representing the Old and New Testaments, or a way to acknowledge the underlying presence and support of the Divine through the trials and changes that human life comprises.

historical_references.reference: The name Celene has been used throughout Christian history by saints, scholars, and faithful believers who exemplified its meaning.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Celene remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
